query: How do reasons for visit relate to urgency and visit duration across department and age group?

per_column.name: visit_type
per_column.rationale: A clean categorization of the reason for visit (preventive, acute, chronic, emergency) that directly relates reasons to urgency/duration. Values match source text well (annual exam→preventive, cough→acute, MI follow-up→chronic).

per_column.name: primary_clinical_category
per_column.rationale: Organ-system/clinical grouping gives a strong new axis for grouping reasons. Values are well-grounded; the annual-exam row mapped to endocrine_metabolic is defensible given HbA1c/lipid focus though arguably preventive.

per_column.name: symptom_acuity
per_column.rationale: Severity gradient is a useful mediator between reason and urgency/duration and distinct from the original urgency field. Values track the text (mild fatigue→mild, asymptomatic follow-up→asymptomatic, moderate acne→moderate).

per_column.name: condition_complexity
per_column.rationale: New vs known/stable/worsening adds analytical leverage for duration/urgency modeling. Well grounded (stable MI→known_stable, worsening acne→known_worsening).

per_column.name: injury_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Etiology axis is useful, but this is essentially duplicated by injury_or_illness_mechanism, reducing marginal value. Values are reasonable readings of the text.

per_column.name: diagnostic_workup_intensity
per_column.rationale: Workup level plausibly correlates with duration, a useful axis. High NULL count is acceptable as 'not stated'. Values grounded (labs→basic_labs, MRI→imaging_ordered).

per_column.name: treatment_intensity
per_column.rationale: Useful for duration/urgency, but somewhat inferential and prone to overreach. The tennis-knee row labeled procedural_in_office is not supported by the text, which only mentions MRI ordered—an invented treatment.

per_column.name: disposition_signal
per_column.rationale: Disposition is a reasonable outcome axis, but often not stated in the text and thus inferred. 'discharge_with_followup' for the acne row is plausible but not explicit; some confident specifics exceed source support.

per_column.name: patient_age_proxy
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with the original age_group column and heavily dominated by 'adult' (near-constant), giving little new analytical leverage. Values are mostly reasonable but partly inferred from department (Pediatrics→toddler).

per_column.name: injury_or_illness_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Near-duplicate of injury_mechanism with nearly identical distribution; a mere restatement adding minimal new leverage. Values themselves are well grounded.

judge.rationale: Most added columns provide genuine new axes (visit_type, clinical_category, symptom_acuity, condition_complexity, workup intensity) that directly serve the query relating reasons to urgency and duration across department/age. Groundedness is generally solid, matching source readings. Weaknesses: two mechanism columns are near-duplicates, patient_age_proxy is largely redundant with the existing age_group and near-constant, and the inferential columns (treatment_intensity, disposition_signal) occasionally assert specifics beyond what the text supports (e.g., a procedural treatment for a knee row that only mentions MRI ordered). Per scope rules, no penalty applied for missing columns.
